title: Finite coefficient filtration preserves constructibility and the cohomological interval
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme with small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $B$ be a finite commutative ring, and let $B_Y$ be its constant sheaf of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $\mathcal R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on this site and $\rho:\mathcal R\to B_Y$ a unital morphism. Let $P$ be an integer-indexed cochain complex of $\mathcal R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] whose terms are flat: tensoring sheaves of $\mathcal R$-modules with $P^q$ is exact for every $q$ [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Let $V$ be a finite $B$-module equipped with a finite decreasing filtration by $B$-submodules $V=V_0\supseteq V_1\supseteq\cdots\supseteq V_t=0$, where $t\ge0$, and write $W_j=V_j/V_{j+1}$ for $0\le j<t$. For any such module $U$, write $U_Y$ for its constant module sheaf, regarded as an $\mathcal R$-module through $\rho$, and put $C_U=P\otimes_{\mathcal R}U_Y$, a complex of $B_Y$-modules, using termwise sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Fix integers $r\le s$ and assume that for every $0\le j<t$ all cohomology sheaves of $C_{W_j}$ are constructible $B_Y$-modules [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] and vanish outside $[r,s]$. Then, for every $0\le j\le t$, all cohomology sheaves of $C_{V_j}$ are constructible $B_Y$-modules and vanish outside the same interval $[r,s]$. In particular this holds for $P\otimes_{\mathcal R}V_Y$, independently of the length $t$ of the filtration.

source.place: Tag 09B5, lemma-constructible-serre; finite coefficient-module filtration and the common cohomological interval are the agent-written devissage application, not an additional assertion of the tag.

proof.text: For $j<t$, the quotient definition gives a short exact sequence of $B$-modules $0\to V_{j+1}\to V_j\to W_j\to0$. Its constant presheaf sequence is exact at every object. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-r-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] with the constant coefficient ring $B$: sheafification is exact and yields $0\to(V_{j+1})_Y\to(V_j)_Y\to(W_j)_Y\to0$. These are the constant sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], with their induced $B_Y$-actions. Restrict those actions through $\rho$ as in [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. This remains exact as a sequence of $\mathcal R$-modules: restriction changes neither the underlying additive sheaves nor the maps, and kernels and sheafified cokernels carry the restricted action by their usual formulas in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Tag 03EI, lemma-sheafification-exact, specialized to the constant ring presheaf B; compare Tag 093J, lemma-constant-exact

proof.text: Apply the assumed exact functor $P^q\otimes_{\mathcal R}-$ to the sequence in step 1 for each $q\in\mathbf Z$. This is precisely the flatness hypothesis, rather than an assertion of flatness for any coefficient quotient [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. The resulting maps are $1\otimes\iota_j$ and $1\otimes\pi_j$. They commute with $d_P^q\otimes1$, since both composites act on local pure tensors as $p\otimes v\mapsto d_P^q(p)\otimes\iota_j(v)$ or $d_P^q(p)\otimes\pi_j(v)$, respectively, and extend through sheafification [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The $B_Y$-action is $b(p\otimes v)=p\otimes bv$; commutativity of $B_Y$ and the scalar map $\rho$ make this well-defined, and all maps are $B_Y$-linear. Exactness is still exactness in $B_Y$-modules: the additive kernels and sheafified cokernels are those of the same maps, with the induced $B_Y$-action [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Thus $0\to C_{V_{j+1}}\to C_{V_j}\to C_{W_j}\to0$ is degreewise short exact in the abelian category $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(B_Y)$ on the given small site.

source.place: Section 03EK, section-tensor-product; application of the exact tensor functors explicitly assumed in the statement

proof.text: Prove the assertion for all $V_j$ by descending induction on $j$, starting at $j=t$. Since $V_t=0$, the complex $C_{V_t}$ is zero: each presheaf tensor $P^q\otimes_{\mathcal R}0$ is zero, and its sheafification is zero [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Its cohomology is zero in every degree. The zero sheaf is constructible in [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]: the single stratum $Y$ has the constant zero module as local model, with finite zero stalks (also when $Y$ is empty). This proves the base case, including $t=0$. For the induction step fix $j<t$ and assume the whole assertion for $V_{j+1}$. The layer $C_{W_j}$ has constructible cohomology and support in $[r,s]$ by the original hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 09B5, lemma-constructible-serre; agent-written descending filtration induction, zero base case

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] in $\mathcal A$ to the degreewise short exact sequence of step 2. For every integer $n$ the segment $H^n(C_{V_{j+1}})\to H^n(C_{V_j})\to H^n(C_{W_j})$ is exact. If $n<r$ or $n>s$, both outside objects are zero by the induction hypothesis and the layer hypothesis. Hence the middle object is zero: its identity factors through its image from the zero left object, since its map to the zero right object has full kernel. This proves the same interval $[r,s]$ for $C_{V_j}$, without shifting either endpoint.

source.place: Tag 0117, lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain, exactness at the middle cohomology object

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle], the sequence in step 2 gives a distinguished triangle $Q(C_{V_{j+1}})\to Q(C_{V_j})\to Q(C_{W_j})\to Q(C_{V_{j+1}})[1]$ in $D(\mathcal A)$. Their cohomology sheaves in the sense of [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] are those of the representing complexes, since $H^n\circ Q\cong H^n$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Both outside vertices have constructible cohomology and only finitely many nonzero cohomology sheaves, since their common interval $[r,s]$ is finite. Apply the middle-vertex closure assertion of [lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated] with $\Lambda=B$ and this very scheme $Y$. It gives constructible cohomology for $C_{V_j}$. This theorem uses exactly the global finite-stratification constructibility in the item and allows every scheme and every finite commutative ring; no Noetherian hypothesis on $Y$ is added. Together with step 4 this completes the induction step. Descending induction gives every $0\le j\le t$, and $V_0=V$ gives the final assertion. The induction never enlarges $[r,s]$, so the bounds are independent of $t$.
